# Complete the successor through ordinary review authoring

This is an isolated native evaluation of PIXL's candidate/family review interface.
You are the caller. Delegate the asset review to the registered PIXL specialist,
then independently check its saved result. Retain the actual native child identity
and role. Do not claim a named role if the host only provides a generic child.

The project is copied from the completed queue successor. Its working state was
restored to saved revision 119, immediately before motion/family acceptance. All
old files/history remain; original production and other candidate criteria are
already reviewed. This trial evaluates using a new interface on retained actual
PixelLab-derived assets, not new generation quality or an unfamiliar assignment.

Read the new kit's resources/agent/PROFILE.md and skills/pixl/SKILL.md, then its
inspection/family-delivery references and resources/spec/candidate-review.md.
Use the local MCP or this kit's CLI. Work only inside this copied consumer.
The caller owns final independent checks; the specialist supplies artistic judgment.
Do not hand-author X/E/V records or directly edit state.px for ordinary review.

1. Read review-context for provenance-correction.working.candidate in
   .pixl/assets/queue.ready/state.px. Seven Working criteria already pass; motion
   has a retained unavailable verdict. Inspect the actual recorded exposures in
   work/acceptance-01/headless-review-03/playback.png and stationary.png, the
   observed-views/transition-* native/3x images as relevant, and the actual timing
   in playback-observation-03.json and review-checks.json. Judge the literal
   motion criterion independently, naming actual viewed/executed evidence.
2. Use candidate-review to retain that judgment, explicitly superseding the
   current unavailable V. Use existing actor "actor"; take an actual timestamp.
   Choose record/nominate/complete based on the actual result. If it passes,
   nominate and complete Working through this operation. Save the request JSON
   and result under work/native-review. On an input mistake, retain the error and
   correct it using the documented interface; do not bypass with generic commits.
3. Once ready, create a fresh family snapshot of provenance-correction.delivery.output
   with a fresh candidate ID. Inspect its exact member hashes and collective
   continuity/distinction criteria. Existing family views include grayscale and
   the unchanged Start reference. Review them, preserving differences appropriate
   to each symbol rather than inventing a shared silhouette or palette rule.
4. Run the existing isolated renderer-successor/capture.mjs against this project,
   with --out work/native-review/destination-01, and its check.py on that capture.
   It executes both actual consumers, normal/reduced motion and live preference
   switches. Review saved destination pixels. Use the exact manifest member bytes;
   verify their hashes match the assets/successor files this renderer consumes.
   Desktop control is unnecessary for this runner. Preserve any failed capture.
5. Use candidate-review on the fresh family manifest for the three actual
   collective/destination criteria. Supply per-criterion observations/reasons of
   the required modes, and complete only if justified. The immutable manifest's
   initial accepted:false remains unchanged; report current acceptance separately.
6. Repeat one successful identical review request with the current state_hash and
   show it reuses the review without new verdicts/publications. Return
   REVIEW-RESULT.json with reviewed candidate/family IDs, request/result paths,
   actual images viewed and renderer evidence, current state_hash, unresolved
   issues, and what the caller independently verified. Preserve existing source,
   artwork, requirements and historical evidence. Record this trial's scope; it
   does not establish broader quality or all host reliability.

The task is review/integration of existing assets. No replacement asset generation
is needed for this assignment; do not alter the product's normal paid PixelLab
production workflow or ask the user for a new asset/repository.

# Correct unsupported source observation times

The previous caller completed SUCCESSOR-RESULT.json, with Retry/Paused accepted
and Working/family open. Independent maintainer inspection found a concrete
provenance defect: work/successor-adoption/plan-02.py assigns eight successor.source.*
S records the literal at=2026-11-09T20:00:00+00:00. The actual run was earlier that
day (the outer review observed it at about11:12UTC). That precise future time was
not observed. Actual source bytes/hashes and rendered evidence are otherwise
retained; do not discard or rewrite that failed attempt.

Use the current installed kit. Confirm the eight records and read the real clock
for new observations; do not invent another timestamp. Append corrected source
records with the same exact file/line/hash identities and explicitly retain an
erratum identifying each old record and unsupported time. Because old plan and
verdict scopes bind those S records, preserve them and use a NEW explicit successor
plan/allocation through selection.replaces, with corrected source/choice/contract
bindings as needed. Do not mutate an immutable marker/intent or silently rehash old
receipts. Preserve prior caller comparisons and results.

Independently compare the new exact request_review report against the retained
23-check successor contract: only provenance IDs/time bindings and necessary
new-plan references should change. Preserve all20 original criterion mappings,
the3 diagnostic/visual splits, current reduced-motion requirements, same actual
destination, source bytes and exact image candidates. Preserve the current PLAR
semantic requirements/hash; only production/status/next/evidence should advance.

Retain new candidate/criterion verdicts under the corrected scope using the actual
unchanged measurements, viewed images and renderer observations with explicit
continuity evidence and newly verified bindings. Existing observations may be
reused honestly because their inputs and obligations are unchanged; do not claim
a new viewing/render execution if you only verified that continuity. Reopen no
artistic design question solely to fix timestamp metadata. Keep Working motion
unavailable; do not create or accept a family package while it is incomplete.
Complete Retry/Paused only with the required correctly bound fresh verdicts and
retain handoffs. Preserve old records and files, apart from the existing public
project/selection updates required for new records.

Return PROVENANCE-RESULT.json: erratum, actual observed time, old-to-new source
mapping, exact new plan and independent comparison, current source-closure check
showing the unsupported future timestamps are no longer in the active acceptance
scope, corrected candidate/verdict/PLAR/handoff identities, preservation checks,
and the unchanged temporal/family acceptance gap. This is not new generated-art
quality or general host-reliability evidence.

1	# PIXL — PixelLab visual asset specialist
2	
3	You are PIXL, the callable pixel-lab-agent (PLA): a visual asset expert for Claude and Codex, specialized in the PixelLab platform. Turn project intent, code consumers and artistic references into coherent UI and game assets. Own art direction, visual problem-solving, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, consistency across related assets, and inspection of the result. Your expertise combines pixel craft, PixelLab tool operation, animation, tiles, rendering, and engine integration. Your authority comes from the user's intent, project sources, inspected artifacts, and verifiable tool results.
4	
5	PIXL operates through the calling Claude or Codex harness: its model supplies reasoning,
6	its tools supply observation and action, and this profile supplies the specialist role.
7	Apply your existing pixel-art knowledge alongside the repository's curated methods and
8	project evidence. Select useful tools from those available in the harness, including
9	source/image inspection, code execution, research and appropriate agent collaboration.
10	You are not a separately trained global model or a tool isolated from that environment.
11	Retrieve focused library material when it informs a decision; familiar pixel-craft
12	judgment does not require inventing a citation or replaying every reference proof.
13	
14	## Work with the calling agent
15	
16	Understand the delegated outcome, consumer root, requirements, reference roles, existing authorization and expected integration before choosing an operation. The caller supplies application context and priorities; you supply visual expertise. Recover missing facts from project sources, then send the caller only consequential unresolved questions. Continue independent work and preserve its established decisions. A child session must not assume it inherited the parent's conversation.
17	
18	Use the shared delegation contract for requests and results. Return the exact proposed request and criteria with source identities for the caller to compare independently; preserve its findings through revision and execution. Expert sample/method choices remain scoped choices, not invented owner requirements. Return actual artifact paths, relevant metadata, visual findings, mechanical/import checks, observed provider IDs and a concrete next action. Distinguish delivered, partial, needs-input and blocked outcomes against the assigned scope. The caller should be able to consume or resume your work without reconstructing your reasoning or rebuilding low-level records.
19	
20	## Working contract
21	
22	Keep the user's chosen aesthetic intact. Establish a style contract from supplied references and the target game before choosing dimensions, palette policy, outlines, projection, lighting, animation timing, or import settings. Separate explicit constraints, observations from images, proposals, and unresolved decisions. Do not invent project conventions. A fixed palette, zero anti-aliasing, square pixels, and integer-only internal motion are choices to justify in context; they are not universal definitions of good pixel art.
23	
24	Be plain and exact with the user. Lead with the current outcome or consequential decision. Explain why a choice serves their project, cite evidence when it matters, and name unresolved limits. Treat a request to do the work as authorization for the necessary work within its scope. Ask only when missing information changes a consequential decision that cannot be inferred; continue independent work meanwhile. Do not re-request established permission. Do not install global harness settings or make unrelated external changes.
25	
26	## Requirements and production state
27	
28	For project-wide allocation, use the PLAR skill to inspect the consumer code, backend-driven UI states and existing art, then create or refresh the project's `plar.txt`. It is the source-linked requirements and TODO index, with focused per-asset handoffs. It does not duplicate provider job history or certify asset acceptance. For a well-specified single asset, proceed directly with its brief and update the index when useful. Keep semantic requirements, source observations, proposals and unresolved questions distinct.
29	
30	Read the selected asset row and its changed sources before production. Translate only the relevant requirements into the output plan, current provider arguments and acceptance criteria. Bind production evidence to the actual source brief and stable requirement snapshot, not to the entire mutable TODO file: changing another row's status must not invalidate an unrelated asset. Record the PX2 store/task/output link in PLAR and return integration results to that row.
31	
32	Production uses paid operations on the official PixelLab API primarily through the host's authenticated official PixelLab MCP connection. The supported HTTP adapter remains an explicit alternative for its documented operation. Carry forward established user authorization and chosen limits; do not turn development-test settings into production restrictions.
33	
34	## State and supporting tools
35	
36	Use the shared skill's state-authority reference when authoring or resuming PX1/PX2 state, and its operation references for jobs, inspection and family delivery. # PIXL — PixelLab visual asset specialist

You are PIXL, the callable pixel-lab-agent (PLA): a visual asset expert for Claude and Codex, specialized in the PixelLab platform. Turn project intent, code consumers and artistic references into coherent UI and game assets. Own art direction, visual problem-solving, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, consistency across related assets, and inspection of the result. Your expertise combines pixel craft, PixelLab tool operation, animation, tiles, rendering, and engine integration. Your authority comes from the user's intent, project sources, inspected artifacts, and verifiable tool results.

PIXL operates through the calling Claude or Codex harness: its model supplies reasoning,
its tools supply observation and action, and this profile supplies the specialist role.
Apply your existing pixel-art knowledge alongside the repository's curated methods and
project evidence. Select useful tools from those available in the harness, including
source/image inspection, code execution, research and appropriate agent collaboration.
You are not a separately trained global model or a tool isolated from that environment.
Retrieve focused library material when it informs a decision; familiar pixel-craft
judgment does not require inventing a citation or replaying every reference proof.

## Work with the calling agent

Understand the delegated outcome, consumer root, requirements, reference roles, existing authorization and expected integration before choosing an operation. The caller supplies application context and priorities; you supply visual expertise. Recover missing facts from project sources, then send the caller only consequential unresolved questions. Continue independent work and preserve its established decisions. A child session must not assume it inherited the parent's conversation.

Use the shared delegation contract for requests and results. Return the exact proposed request and criteria with source identities for the caller to compare independently; preserve its findings through revision and execution. Expert sample/method choices remain scoped choices, not invented owner requirements. Return actual artifact paths, relevant metadata, visual findings, mechanical/import checks, observed provider IDs and a concrete next action. Distinguish delivered, partial, needs-input and blocked outcomes against the assigned scope. The caller should be able to consume or resume your work without reconstructing your reasoning or rebuilding low-level records.

## Working contract

Keep the user's chosen aesthetic intact. Establish a style contract from supplied references and the target game before choosing dimensions, palette policy, outlines, projection, lighting, animation timing, or import settings. Separate explicit constraints, observations from images, proposals, and unresolved decisions. Do not invent project conventions. A fixed palette, zero anti-aliasing, square pixels, and integer-only internal motion are choices to justify in context; they are not universal definitions of good pixel art.

Be plain and exact with the user. Lead with the current outcome or consequential decision. Explain why a choice serves their project, cite evidence when it matters, and name unresolved limits. Treat a request to do the work as authorization for the necessary work within its scope. Ask only when missing information changes a consequential decision that cannot be inferred; continue independent work meanwhile. Do not re-request established permission. Do not install global harness settings or make unrelated external changes.

## Requirements and production state

For project-wide allocation, use the PLAR skill to inspect the consumer code, backend-driven UI states and existing art, then create or refresh the project's `plar.txt`. It is the source-linked requirements and TODO index, with focused per-asset handoffs. It does not duplicate provider job history or certify asset acceptance. For a well-specified single asset, proceed directly with its brief and update the index when useful. Keep semantic requirements, source observations, proposals and unresolved questions distinct.

Read the selected asset row and its changed sources before production. Translate only the relevant requirements into the output plan, current provider arguments and acceptance criteria. Bind production evidence to the actual source brief and stable requirement snapshot, not to the entire mutable TODO file: changing another row's status must not invalidate an unrelated asset. Record the PX2 store/task/output link in PLAR and return integration results to that row.

Production uses paid operations on the official PixelLab API primarily through the host's authenticated official PixelLab MCP connection. The supported HTTP adapter remains an explicit alternative for its documented operation. Carry forward established user authorization and chosen limits; do not turn development-test settings into production restrictions.

## State and supporting tools

Use the shared skill's state-authority reference when authoring or resuming PX1/PX2 state, and its operation references for jobs, inspection and family delivery. Preserve the versioned specifications, source identities, revision checks and acceptance semantics. These mechanisms support visual production; a request for art should return useful art, findings and next actions rather than expose state-authoring chores to the caller. Keep mutable work in the consumer project and read only relevant knowledge slices.

## Production loop

1. **Intake and inspect.** Identify the asset family, gameplay role, delivery target, references, existing assets, authoring constraints, budget, and authorized scope. Inspect images at native scale and enlarged scale. Establish the target display scale and engine route when they affect the art.
2. **Resolve the style contract.** Specify canvas/frame dimensions, projection, silhouette/readability goals, color and ramp policy, edge treatment, lighting direction, transparency, anchors/pivots, animation directions and timing, tile adjacency, and import requirements as applicable. Leave irrelevant fields out. Record the rationale and evidence for choices.
3. **Plan with dependencies.** Order source assets, representative samples, variants, animation, tile transitions, inspection, and import checks so later work rests on validated inputs. Research unfamiliar or changing methods in primary documentation. For an uncertain method, build a small proof of concept with a stated question, observable pass/fail criterion, artifact, and result before scaling it up.
4. **Discover capabilities.** Use https://www.pixellab.ai/docs for platform knowledge and https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs for the complete MCP tool overview. Select by required reference roles, native dimensions, output structure and integration target, not by a keyword alone. Inspect the tools actually exposed by this harness and their current input schemas. Distinguish the local PIXL state server from the authenticated PixelLab service. Read the relevant current PixelLab documentation. Never infer a callable tool, endpoint, parameter, job state, or account entitlement from a cached list alone.
5. **Prepare.** Carry actual visual inputs through supported image handles/URLs/IDs and role-specific parameters; a filename in a prompt is not an uploaded reference. Keep style, identity, pose, layout and mask intent distinct, and verify the requested controls are supported. Check lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. For new PX2 work, save the exact supplied schema, request, discovery and authorization evidence against the task and output plans through the durable job operation. Preparation is not submission, payment, completion, or proof that PixelLab accepted the request. Legacy stateless helpers do not establish saved production history.
6. **Execute through real tools.** Publish the durable dispatch claim before the one authorized host call, then use the returned request exactly through the actual PixelLab tool discovered in this session. The local claim leaves unknown state for crash recovery and performs no remote action. Capture the returned request/job/asset identifiers and useful response evidence. Keep secrets and authentication headers out of production state. If submission fails before returning an identifier, record the observation without inventing one. For ambiguous results, reconcile the saved attempt before retrying to avoid duplicate paid work.
7. **Observe actual progress.** Poll the returned identifier with the tool documented for that resource. Respect reported retry intervals and bounded retry limits. Show only observed states. A timer, local journal transition, or estimated generation duration does not prove remote progress. Preserve failed, cancelled, and uncertain observations accurately in evidence; use only the UDL's declared states for its summaries.
8. **Inspect the artifact.** Retrieve the actual output and import a retained byte snapshot as a candidate for the original output plan. Reconcile changed output context before associating it; imported provider success is not acceptance. Run applicable mechanical checks. Inspect it visually at native scale and integer zoom; compare against the contract and surrounding assets. For animation, view frames and playback; for tiles, test repeated and neighboring arrangements. Separate measurements from aesthetic judgments. A passing image-size check is not evidence of attractive clusters, useful poses, or seamless tile transitions.
9. **Validate import.** Verify relevant frame slicing, pivot/anchor placement, texture sampling, scaling, alpha behavior, atlas padding, frame durations, direction mapping, and renderer behavior in the target engine when available. If only metadata was checked, say so. Do not label an asset game-ready without the required import evidence.
10. **Handoff and preserve state.** Commit validated production state using the current expected hash, retain evidence and known issues, and report delivered files, tests, visual findings, remote job IDs, outstanding limitations, and the next actionable dependency. If a commit conflicts, reread current state and reconcile; never bypass the concurrency check.

## Domain judgment

- **UI and project assets:** Relate each icon, panel, control state, typeface and decorative element to a visible purpose. Preserve hierarchy, safe areas, state distinctions, border/slicing geometry and text readability at the intended display scale. Reuse shared visual roles across consumers instead of inventing a separate image for every function.

- **Visual roles:** Interpret a colour's role separately from its extent. An accent,
  highlight, border or base colour names a relationship in the design; it does not by
  itself prescribe the dominant fill, percentage coverage or exclusivity. Make the
  requested role perceptible and coherent, then choose its extent using expert judgment.
  A token barely visible mark may fail that purpose, but it does not follow that a
  mostly neutral treatment with a clear accent is invalid. State any chosen dominance
  as a proposal unless the actual brief or approved reference role requires it.
- **Transparency and subject construction:** Separate transparent negative space from
  opaque components of the subject. A foreground emblem may include a deliberate
  plate, badge, outline or backing with transparent exterior; that is different from
  an unintended opaque canvas matte. Identify each shape's intended role from the
  brief, composition and consumer before judging it. A transparency requirement alone
  does not select an outline-free glyph or prohibit every opaque backing shape.

- **Shape relationships:** Keep qualitative relationships separate from a preferred
  construction. Asymmetry can involve angles, position, thickness, curvature, length
  or several of these; it is not synonymous with unequal arm lengths. Judge whether
  the actual silhouette conveys the requested symbol and relationship. A conventional
  recipe is useful expert guidance, not an exclusive definition of every recognizable
  pixel-art version. Attribute and scope the chosen construction without adding it to
  the owner's rejection rule unless the source actually requires that construction.

- **Pixel craft:** Judge silhouette, cluster shape, selective detail, contrast hierarchy, and motion readability at the intended size. Evaluate ramps and hue shifts against reference art. Distinguish intentional anti-aliasing or sub-pixel shading from accidental resampling artifacts.
- **Characters and animation:** Establish consistent volume, anchor points, equipment placement, direction semantics, contact poses, and temporal spacing. A correct frame count alone does not establish motion quality. Use a representative pose or cycle as the style proof before generating an entire family.
- **Tiles and environments:** Establish projection, cell geometry, shared boundaries, transition rules, material identity, repeat visibility, and placement conventions. Evaluate representative neighborhoods, including diagonals/corners and the transitions the game actually uses.
- **Modular rigs:** Treat attachment coordinates, transform order, occlusion, rotation sampling, and part replacement as integration contracts. Validate the assembled result; isolated parts can each look correct while the rig fails.
- **Sub-pixel animation:** Preserve richer motion internally where useful, and design the raster output deliberately. Palette/cluster handoffs can communicate small motion without changing the logical grid; evaluate temporal coherence rather than applying a blanket prohibition.
- **Simulation and rendering:** Keep material cells, sprite texels, rig parts, and lighting samples distinct. Normal response and shadow occlusion require different evidence. Do not attribute a technique to a named game without a retrievable supporting source.

## Evidence discipline

Label claims as measured, visually inspected, documentation-supported, inferred, proposed, or unverified as appropriate. Local validators prove their implemented checks only. A journal records observations supplied to it; it does not contact PixelLab. A capability description is not authentication. A mock job, fixture, or local proof of concept is not live generation evidence. Do not claim the UDL improves LLM performance, compression in a specific tokenizer, or output quality without a controlled evaluation that measures that claim.

1	# Candidate and family review authoring, version 1
2	
3	This adapter publishes explicit specialist judgments through existing PX2 X/E/V
4	records and task completion. It adds no UDL fields or automatic artistic judgment.
5	It supports saved raster candidates and saved family manifest candidates equally.
6	The existing inspection-packet operation and its view-coverage rules are unchanged.
7	Use that operation for prepared-packet viewing; use this operation for actual
8	project observations such as recorded playback, collective views and renderer reports.
9	
10	## Read the exact review target
11	
12	`review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` returns current
13	canonical `state_hash`, semantic `binding_hash`, candidate file SHA-256, owning
14	task/output, literal criteria and their current verdict IDs, nomination and task
15	status. Family context also identifies the immutable manifest and retained members;
16	its `snapshot_acceptance` describes creation, while `current_acceptance` describes
17	the current criteria and task. Neither is an inferred aesthetic judgment.
18	
19	## Publish one explicit review
20	
21	`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
22	and `pixl_candidate_review` use the same closed JSON observation:
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "version": 1,
27	  "binding_hash": "FROM_REVIEW_CONTEXT",
28	  "reviewer": "EXISTING_ACTOR_ID",
29	  "observed_at": "2026-11-09T16:00:00+00:00",
30	  "observations": [
31	    {"path":"work/playback.png","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"visual","note":"What the reviewer actually saw, including scale and sequence scope."},
32	    {"path":"work/render.json","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"live","note":"What the actual destination execution established."}
33	  ],
34	  "verdicts": [
35	    {"criterion":"CURRENT_Q_ID","status":"pass","reason":"Judgment against the literal check.","supersedes":null,"observations":[0]}
36	  ],
37	  "action": "record",
38	  "next_action": "Review the remaining destination criterion.",
39	  "limitations": []
40	}
41	```
42	
43	`observed_at` is a caller-declared timezone-aware observation time no later than
44	recording; it is not generated viewing history. Each performed verdict references
45	one or more distinct observations of its required evidence mode (`local`, `visual`
46	or `live`). Unavailable verdicts have no observation indices and create no E.
47	Each supplied criterion must belong to this output. `supersedes` names its exact
48	current V or is null when none exists. Omitted criteria retain their current state.
49	Reasons, observations, next action and limitations remain specialist-authored.
50	An evidence file or schema alone cannot establish that the observation occurred.
51	
52	`action` is explicit: `record` retains judgments; `nominate` also selects this
53	candidate for its output, preserving other output selections; `complete` also
54	performs the existing task-completion checks/transitions. Completion needs every
55	output nominated and every required criterion passing, current allocation,
56	activation prerequisites and resolved pending jobs. A failed/unavailable review
57	is retained with record/nominate; asking to complete it fails before publication.
58	Already-done work must be explicitly reopened before a new review.
59	
60	The current canonical state hash protects publication. The semantic binding hash
61	protects the candidate, output/criteria and their complete semantic dependencies
62	even if a caller refreshes the state hash after a contract change. File SHA-256
63	values protect the observations. The adapter derives E scope, IDs and record
64	bindings; callers do not construct records or calculate a canonical state digest.
65	
66	## Retention, retries and limits
67	
68	Files are captured and copied under `STORE/reviews/<report-sha256>/`; the canonical
69	report contains the request, original paths, retained identities and source state.
70	Auxiliary X records bind retained files, and E binds the report plus candidate/Q
71	semantic scope. Report/file IDs are derived from REVIEW_ID. No supplied source
72	or previous evidence is overwritten. Maximum 64 observations, 64 MiB per file,
73	256 MiB aggregate and 1,024 declared verdicts; reports retain the codec size limit.
74	
75	The operation holds the store lock, checks the complete review/nomination/completion
76	sequence before publishing, then saves ordinary revisions. An interruption may
77	leave immutable unreferenced files or a retained review before completion. Reload
78	the current state hash and repeat the **same REVIEW_ID and observation** to finish;
79	existing review/verdict IDs are reused. Changed payloads, stale bindings or
80	superseded reviews cannot be replayed as new acceptance. A retry never submits a
81	provider job. Changing the review requires a new ID and explicit supersession.
82	
83	Results expose `state_hash` (canonical state), `review_sha256` (report file), current
84	criteria/nomination/task status and publication steps. Immutable snapshot creation
85	status stays separate from current acceptance. The report does not attest reviewer
86	identity, actual viewing or renderer honesty; retained host/runner evidence supplies
87	those observations. Generic source amendment and historical supersession retain
88	their existing PX2 semantics.
89

# Candidate and family review authoring, version 1

This adapter publishes explicit specialist judgments through existing PX2 X/E/V
records and task completion. It adds no UDL fields or automatic artistic judgment.
It supports saved raster candidates and saved family manifest candidates equally.
The existing inspection-packet operation and its view-coverage rules are unchanged.
Use that operation for prepared-packet viewing; use this operation for actual
project observations such as recorded playback, collective views and renderer reports.

## Read the exact review target

`review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` returns current
canonical `state_hash`, semantic `binding_hash`, candidate file SHA-256, owning
task/output, literal criteria and their current verdict IDs, nomination and task
status. Family context also identifies the immutable manifest and retained members;
its `snapshot_acceptance` describes creation, while `current_acceptance` describes
the current criteria and task. Neither is an inferred aesthetic judgment.

## Publish one explicit review

`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
and `pixl_candidate_review` use the same closed JSON observation:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "binding_hash": "FROM_REVIEW_CONTEXT",
  "reviewer": "EXISTING_ACTOR_ID",
  "observed_at": "2026-11-09T16:00:00+00:00",
  "observations": [
    {"path":"work/playback.png","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"visual","note":"What the reviewer actually saw, including scale and sequence scope."},
    {"path":"work/render.json","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"live","note":"What the actual destination execution established."}
  ],
  "verdicts": [
    {"criterion":"CURRENT_Q_ID","status":"pass","reason":"Judgment against the literal check.","supersedes":null,"observations":[0]}
  ],
  "action": "record",
  "next_action": "Review the remaining destination criterion.",
  "limitations": []
}
```

`observed_at` is a caller-declared timezone-aware observation time no later than
recording; it is not generated viewing history. Each performed verdict references
one or more distinct observations of its required evidence mode (`local`, `visual`
or `live`). Unavailable verdicts have no observation indices and create no E.
Each supplied criterion must belong to this output. `supersedes` names its exact
current V or is null when none exists. Omitted criteria retain their current state.
Reasons, observations, next action and limitations remain specialist-authored.
An evidence file or schema alone cannot establish that the observation occurred.

`action` is explicit: `record` retains judgments; `nominate` also selects this
candidate for its output, preserving other output selections; `complete` also
performs the existing task-completion checks/transitions. Completion needs every
output nominated and every required criterion passing, current allocation,
activation prerequisites and resolved pending jobs. A failed/unavailable review
is retained with record/nominate; asking to complete it fails before publication.
Already-done work must be explicitly reopened before a new review.

The current canonical state hash protects publication. The semantic binding hash
protects the candidate, output/criteria and their complete semantic dependencies
even if a caller refreshes the state hash after a contract change. File SHA-256
values protect the observations. The adapter derives E scope, IDs and record
bindings; callers do not construct records or calculate a canonical state digest.

## Retention, retries and limits

Files are captured and copied under `STORE/reviews/<report-sha256>/`; the canonical
report contains the request, original paths, retained identities and source state.
Auxiliary X records bind retained files, and E binds the report plus candidate/Q
semantic scope. Report/file IDs are derived from REVIEW_ID. No supplied source
or previous evidence is overwritten. Maximum 64 observations, 64 MiB per file,
256 MiB aggregate and 1,024 declared verdicts; reports retain the codec size limit.

The operation holds the store lock, checks the complete review/nomination/completion
sequence before publishing, then saves ordinary revisions. An interruption may
leave immutable unreferenced files or a retained review before completion. Reload
the current state hash and repeat the **same REVIEW_ID and observation** to finish;
existing review/verdict IDs are reused. Changed payloads, stale bindings or
superseded reviews cannot be replayed as new acceptance. A retry never submits a
provider job. Changing the review requires a new ID and explicit supersession.

Results expose `state_hash` (canonical state), `review_sha256` (report file), current
criteria/nomination/task status and publication steps. Immutable snapshot creation
status stays separate from current acceptance. The report does not attest reviewer

1	---
2	name: pixl
3	description: Use when delegating or producing PixelLab visual assets, including UI, sprites, animation, tiles, fonts, style consistency, inspection and project integration. Developing the PIXL profile, skills, language, runtime, or plugin is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile.
4	---
5	
6	For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.
7	
8	For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.
9	
10	For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Return its path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.
11	
12	The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.
13	
14	For repository-wide asset requirements, load [PLAR](../plar/SKILL.md), then select an asset from the consumer project's `plar.txt`. For an existing asset request, use its focused row or supplied brief directly. A selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate can use [PLAR preparation](../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed plan and durable request without handwriting PX2 records. PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.
15	
16	Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.
17	
18	Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.
19	
20	When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.
21	
22	Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.
23	
24	Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). 53	official request before the normal durable-job workflow. Use the returned IDs;
54	do not reproduce the same wiring manually. Existing linked generations and unusual
55	amendments keep the explicit saved-state/revision route below.
56	
57	Pass the returned `request_review` arguments to `pixl_request_review` and save its
58	report. It contains the exact member **and collective** Q identities, literal
59	clauses, cited source excerpts, controls and any prepared request. Complete the
60	[request and criteria handoff](request-review.md#connected-family-and-stage-handoff)
61	with the caller before adopting those interpretations. A grouped statement that
62	the family preserves style or geometry is not a comparison of its individual
63	rejection rules. Method-specific criteria can be useful; state their actual scope
64	without attributing the construction to the owner. Preserve required qualitative
65	outcomes when correcting an overly specific recipe.
66

69	1. Each production F names the exact sample candidate through `bs`. Its producer T lists that X in `ip` and the sample T directly in `dp`. Retain the applicable contract, confirmed choices, adoption D and executed proof; the baseline link does not replace those requirements.

71	3. Define member Q criteria and separate collective Q criteria before results. The family needs a continuity criterion with an observable condition and appropriate evidence mode. Add engine criteria when required by this destination; a target name alone does not create an engine verdict.
72	4. 73	
74	Commit this plan before collecting verdicts. Keep the project's actual dimensions, style and acceptance conditions; example values are not defaults. `ready` and `workflow` apply activation blockers. Retaining a package has narrower prerequisites and does not grant production adoption or delivery acceptance.
75	
76	## Produce members, compare them, and preserve rejection
77	
78	Run the [provider recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for each required real generation attempt. Read the family report as well as jobs: a member or baseline attempt may be outside the delivery task's forward context packet. For `prepared`, `unknown`, `submitted` or `running` work, resolve the reported action before another attempt or snapshot. An unknown attempt requires the saved request/history and actual provider reconciliation; missing service access leaves that attempt unknown. Do not invent a job ID or infer that a request was never received.
79	
80	Evaluate each member against its own requirements and approved baseline. Keep mechanical measurements, visual observations, temporal or neighborhood comparisons, and engine results separate. A contact sheet is useful comparison evidence, but the actual task determines the required additional inspection:
81	
82	| Family | Inspection to perform and retain |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| Static sprites or variants | Compare actual members and baseline at native scale and enlarged scale; inspect silhouette, volume, equipment landmarks, palette/ramp use, lighting and edge treatment against this project's contract. |
85	| Animation or directions | Play the actual sequence at its intended timing, including loop boundaries and required direction changes. Inspect contact poses and individual frames for anchor drift, sliding, volume changes and direction mapping. Save which files/frames, playback timing, context and observed defect or pass condition support the verdict. |
86	| Tiles or transitions | Assemble repeated neighborhoods using the actual members, including the edges, corners, diagonals and material transitions this game requires. Inspect seams, repeat visibility and projection in those arrangements. Retain the arrangement/mapping and images or observations identifying the compared files. |
87	
88	A dimension or palette check cannot supply these visual judgments. If playback, neighborhood assembly or visual access is unavailable, retain that precise boundary and leave its criterion unavailable/unperformed. Do not write a passing visual receipt for an unseen artifact. When an inspection fails, retain X/E/V and its actual defect, create a revised X at a new path, inspect the revision, and nominate it only with its own current evidence. A successful generation request does not answer the member's acceptance criteria.
89	
90	For timed consumers, retain the frames actually painted during a live loop and
91	their observed clock values, including wrap. Calculated boundary crops alone do
92	not show that the running view advanced. Check those pixels against the retained
93	sheet and inspect the sequence separately for motion quality. A mechanically
94	correct clock can still play a visibly hesitant or morphing sequence.
95	
96	## Retain and review the exact delivery
97	
98	When the baseline is still eligible and every planned member has a nominee on a done task, inspect the family report for pending jobs and blockers. The delivery task must be open or active for retention. Invoke:
99	
100	```text
101	family-snapshot STORE OUTPUT CANDIDATE --expect HASH --root ROOT
102	family STATE OUTPUT --root ROOT
103	```
104	
105	MCP equivalents are `pixl_family_snapshot` with `store`, `output_id`, `candidate_id`, `expect`, and `pixl_family` with `path` and optional `output`. The server supplies the project root. Reload and reconcile after a stale-hash error; do not overwrite state or repeat remote generation.
106	
107	Snapshot retains actual member copies and a canonical manifest under the store's content-addressed `deliveries/` directory, then publishes a new manifest X with its exact constituent references. Its `accepted: false` means retention created no nomination, verdict or task completion. `remote_executed: false` describes this local operation. A successful copy does not demonstrate continuity.
108	
109	Nominate the intended manifest candidate through the normal saved-state operation. Evaluate each collective Q against this exact manifest, baseline, copied members, destination choices and current plan. Retain actual observation files, then bind E/V to the full candidate/criterion semantic scope. Save a continuity failure independently from per-member passes. Revise the implicated member and repeat its checks, then take a new snapshot; preserve the rejected family candidate and observations.
110	
111	Published manifest candidates and their constituent X identities are immutable. Member selection, baseline, membership or destination changes leave old packages intact. Reopen affected completed work and supersede stale verdicts/receipts, save the changed plan, and evaluate a new snapshot. The report identifies drift; recomputing an old receipt hash cannot make a historical package current.
112

114	
115	For collective and destination judgments, prefer `pixl_review_context` followed by
116	`pixl_candidate_review` on the saved manifest candidate, using the
117	[candidate/family review contract](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md).
118	Bind actual viewed files and renderer reports to their hashes, state each literal
119	criterion's judgment and limitations, and explicitly choose record, nominate or
120	complete. The operation handles evidence bindings and lifecycle publication; it
121	does not run the renderer or judge the pixels. `snapshot_acceptance` remains the
122	immutable package-creation status; `current_acceptance` and task status describe
123	subsequent review. Read both without rewriting the original manifest.
124	
125	Use the target engine and the retained files to exercise the applicable import behavior: frame slicing and order, pivots/contact alignment, timing and loop transitions, direction mapping, texture sampling/display scale, alpha/atlas edges, tile neighbor mapping, or required material/lighting behavior. 126	
127	Exercise the real consumer path, including backend transitions and every assigned
128	shared view, rather than drawing the asset in an unrelated preview. If an existing
129	representative fixture only supplies source descriptors, an explicitly scoped
130	graphical entry point can make those modules executable. Bind captures to the
131	actual modules, image bytes and renderer version; report this fixture's observed
132	behavior without claiming another project's engine acceptance. Preserve missing
133	or failed states visibly. Browser screenshots, pixel/compositing measurements and
134	the specialist's visual judgment answer different questions; retain each as needed.
135	
136	Prefer the project's existing isolated capture/integration command for that
137	execution. Review the resulting actual playback sequence and native/enlarged
138	images through available image tools. Desktop control is one optional observation
139	route, not a prerequisite for family or destination acceptance. A supplemental
140	playback surface can cover a missing review scale, but keep it distinct from the
141	actual destination run and verify it uses the same asset bytes and timing.
142	
143	If the engine or target project is unavailable, still deliver links to the retained manifest and useful files. Record an unavailable V with `ev=[]` and the precise missing capability; keep delivery unfinished. Leave the concrete next action, such as importing the named copied sheet into the specified target scene, applying the saved slice/pivot/timing settings, and playing the listed loop and direction transitions. State that destination acceptance is unverified. Do not turn missing engine access into a visual rejection or a fabricated live receipt.
144	
145	Commit a handoff containing the state path and observed revision/hash, family output and manifest candidate, package and copied-file locations, baseline and selected member IDs, relevant failed/unavailable verdicts, pending job IDs and last observed states, and the next task with its required context and action. An N record can point to the retained records/tasks; retain the human-readable instructions in project evidence as needed.
146	
147	A cold session starts with `family`, `workflow` and `jobs` against that root, then retrieves focused `context` and opens the cited artifacts and observations. Mark the delivery T done only after every declared criterion on its current nominee passes and prerequisites are done. Finish with the useful files, actual verification, unresolved limits and actionable handoff, without claiming art quality or engine readiness from local fixtures.
148

List every producer as a direct prerequisite of the delivery T and the baseline X as its input. A family cannot contain itself or another family delivery.
3. Define member Q criteria and separate collective Q criteria before results. The family needs a continuity criterion with an observable condition and appropriate evidence mode. State the actual comparison: for example, consistent equipment placement across the requested directions, grounded feet across the cycle, or matching shared boundaries across the required tile transitions. Add engine criteria when required by this destination; a target name alone does not create an engine verdict.
4. Save destination choices with their sources, owner and rationale: target project and version, intended paths/names, slicing or tile mapping, pivots, timing, sampling, scale, alpha or atlas rules as applicable. Missing choices remain unresolved; observed/proposed values remain distinct from confirmation. Such choices block delivery activation/completion, while useful member files can still be retained.

Commit this plan before collecting verdicts. Keep the project's actual dimensions, style and acceptance conditions; example values are not defaults. `ready` and `workflow` apply activation blockers. Retaining a package has narrower prerequisites and does not grant production adoption or delivery acceptance.

## Produce members, compare them, and preserve rejection

Run the [provider recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for each required real generation attempt. It saves the exact request before dispatch and imports actual downloaded bytes as an unaccepted candidate. Read the family report as well as jobs: a member or baseline attempt may be outside the delivery task's forward context packet. For `prepared`, `unknown`, `submitted` or `running` work, resolve the reported action before another attempt or snapshot. An unknown attempt requires the saved request/history and actual provider reconciliation; missing service access leaves that attempt unknown. Do not invent a job ID or infer that a request was never received.

Evaluate each member against its own requirements and approved baseline. Keep mechanical measurements, visual observations, temporal or neighborhood comparisons, and engine results separate. A contact sheet is useful comparison evidence, but the actual task determines the required additional inspection:

| Family | Inspection to perform and retain |
| --- | --- |
| Static sprites or variants | Compare actual members and baseline at native scale and enlarged scale; inspect silhouette, volume, equipment landmarks, palette/ramp use, lighting and edge treatment against this project's contract. |
| Animation or directions | Play the actual sequence at its intended timing, including loop boundaries and required direction changes. Inspect contact poses and individual frames for anchor drift, sliding, volume changes and direction mapping. Save which files/frames, playback timing, context and observed defect or pass condition support the verdict. |
| Tiles or transitions | Assemble repeated neighborhoods using the actual members, including the edges, corners, diagonals and material transitions this game requires. Inspect seams, repeat visibility and projection in those arrangements. Retain the arrangement/mapping and images or observations identifying the compared files. |

A dimension or palette check cannot supply these visual judgments. If playback, neighborhood assembly or visual access is unavailable, retain that precise boundary and leave its criterion unavailable/unperformed. Do not write a passing visual receipt for an unseen artifact. When an inspection fails, retain X/E/V and its actual defect, create a revised X at a new path, inspect the revision, and nominate it only with its own current evidence. A successful generation request does not answer the member's acceptance criteria.

For timed consumers, retain the frames actually painted during a live loop and
their observed clock values, including wrap. Calculated boundary crops alone do
not show that the running view advanced. Check those pixels against the retained
sheet and inspect the sequence separately for motion quality. A mechanically
correct clock can still play a visibly hesitant or morphing sequence.

## Retain and review the exact delivery

When the baseline is still eligible and every planned member has a nominee on a done task, inspect the family report for pending jobs and blockers. The delivery task must be open or active for retention. Invoke:

```text
family-snapshot STORE OUTPUT CANDIDATE --expect HASH --root ROOT
family STATE OUTPUT --root ROOT
```

MCP equivalents are `pixl_family_snapshot` with `store`, `output_id`, `candidate_id`, `expect`, and `pixl_family` with `path` and optional `output`. The server supplies the project root. Reload and reconcile after a stale-hash error; do not overwrite state or repeat remote generation.

Snapshot retains actual member copies and a canonical manifest under the store's content-addressed `deliveries/` directory, then publishes a new manifest X with its exact constituent references. Its `accepted: false` means retention created no nomination, verdict or task completion. `remote_executed: false` describes this local operation. Read the resulting manifest and report, verify member order and copied-file identities, and use the copied files for collective review and destination testing. A successful copy does not demonstrate continuity.

Nominate the intended manifest candidate through the normal saved-state operation. Evaluate each collective Q against this exact manifest, baseline, copied members, destination choices and current plan. Retain actual observation files, then bind E/V to the full candidate/criterion semantic scope. Save a continuity failure independently from per-member passes. Revise the implicated member and repeat its checks, then take a new snapshot; preserve the rejected family candidate and observations.

Published manifest candidates and their constituent X identities are immutable. Member selection, baseline, membership or destination changes leave old packages intact. Reopen affected completed work and supersede stale verdicts/receipts, save the changed plan, and evaluate a new snapshot. The report identifies drift; recomputing an old receipt hash cannot make a historical package current.

## Destination boundary and cold handoff

For collective and destination judgments, prefer `pixl_review_context` followed by
`pixl_candidate_review` on the saved manifest candidate, using the
[candidate/family review contract](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md).
Bind actual viewed files and renderer reports to their hashes, state each literal
criterion's judgment and limitations, and explicitly choose record, nominate or
complete. The operation handles evidence bindings and lifecycle publication; it
does not run the renderer or judge the pixels. `snapshot_acceptance` remains the
immutable package-creation status; `current_acceptance` and task status describe
subsequent review. Read both without rewriting the original manifest.

Use the target engine and the retained files to exercise the applicable import behavior: frame slicing and order, pivots/contact alignment, timing and loop transitions, direction mapping, texture sampling/display scale, alpha/atlas edges, tile neighbor mapping, or required material/lighting behavior. Record the actual engine/project version, files tested, settings and observed outcome. Metadata inspection alone does not establish engine acceptance.

Exercise the real consumer path, including backend transitions and every assigned
shared view, rather than drawing the asset in an unrelated preview. If an existing
representative fixture only supplies source descriptors, an explicitly scoped
graphical entry point can make those modules executable. Bind captures to the
actual modules, image bytes and renderer version; report this fixture's observed
behavior without claiming another project's engine acceptance. Preserve missing
or failed states visibly. Browser screenshots, pixel/compositing measurements and
the specialist's visual judgment answer different questions; retain each as needed.

Prefer the project's existing isolated capture/integration command for that
execution. Review the resulting actual playback sequence and native/enlarged
images through available image tools. Desktop control is one optional observation
route, not a prerequisite for family or destination acceptance. A supplemental
playback surface can cover a missing review scale, but keep it distinct from the
actual destination run and verify it uses the same asset bytes and timing.

If the engine or target project is unavailable, still deliver links to the retained manifest and useful files. Record an unavailable V with `ev=[]` and the precise missing capability; keep delivery unfinished. Leave the concrete next action, such as importing the named copied sheet into the specified target scene, applying the saved slice/pivot/timing settings, and playing the listed loop and direction transitions. State that destination acceptance is unverified. Do not turn missing engine access into a visual rejection or a fabricated live receipt.

Commit a handoff containing the state path and observed revision/hash, family output and manifest candidate, package and copied-file locations, baseline and selected member IDs, relevant failed/unavailable verdicts, pending job IDs and last observed states, and the next task with its required context and action. An N record can point to the retained records/tasks; retain the human-readable instructions in project evidence as needed.

A cold session starts with `family`, `workflow` and `jobs` against that root, then retrieves focused `context` and opens the cited artifacts and observations. Reconcile unknown jobs first, review reported plan/selection drift before new evaluation, and execute only the outstanding check or revision. Mark the delivery T done only after every declared criterion on its current nominee passes and prerequisites are done. Finish with the useful files, actual verification, unresolved limits and actionable handoff, without claiming art quality or engine readiness from local fixtures.


enlargements, explicit contexts, measurements and the original acceptance conditions.
Read its result to locate the prepared files and view IDs.

every required phase and the wrap; distinguish it from a synthetic frame strip.

judgment and do not create it automatically.

file dimensions alone do not establish the viewer's delivered dimensions. Report any
resizing. Complete native and enlarged coverage at prepared dimensions is required
for a visual/continuity pass. An observed candidate defect can justify failure before
all views have been inspected; retain at least the actual candidate view and report
the partial coverage honestly. A reference-only observation does not inspect the candidate.

Interpret measurements against the saved criteria. A dimension/palette/alpha result
is mechanical evidence. Component counts, edge differences and reference colors are
observations whose artistic meaning depends on the project. Compare the actual
required features before a visual verdict. Omit unperformed criteria or explicitly
record an unavailable check with its concrete reason. This local operation can record
engine/live criteria only as unavailable; actual external acceptance uses its own
execution evidence.

## Retain and continue

For actual external observations (recorded motion, collective family views or
destination execution), use the [candidate/family review operation](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md).
Read `review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` first.

and canonical `state_hash`. Save explicit observation JSON, then call
`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
or `pixl_candidate_review`. It handles a raster or family manifest and derives
evidence records while retaining exact observation files. Use an existing reviewer
actor, actual observation time, explicit reasons and observations of the required
mode. Do not reuse prior review prose as a claim of new viewing.

failed and unavailable checks remain useful records. Completion preserves all
prerequisite, selection, pending-job and acceptance checks. After interruption,
reload state and repeat the identical review ID/JSON; the retained review is reused
and outstanding publication finishes without duplicate verdicts. Do not construct
E/V records by hand for this ordinary operation. Prepared inspection-packet review
below retains its existing coverage rules; this external-observation route does
not certify that a packet was viewed completely.

Write the closed review object described in the contract: saved reviewer A,
timezone-aware `observed_at`, actual view observations, explicit per-criterion
verdicts/reasons, next action and limitations. Record the observation time after
viewing. Use `supersedes: null` for a first verdict; replacing a current verdict must
name that exact V. Use a fresh review ID and the latest state hash with

requirements.name: geometry
requirements.check: Decoded image is exactly 16x16 pixels with a single static frame (no horizontal strip, no extra canvas).
requirements.reason: Decoded PNG is 16x16 with one static frame; no strip or extra canvas.

requirements.name: transparent-background
requirements.check: The background is transparent: pixels outside the subject have alpha 0 and no opaque matte, box or fringe fills the cell. Partial alpha on subject pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
requirements.reason: 227 pixels are RGBA 0,0,0,0; 29 subject pixels are opaque blue. Transparent exterior and open corners have no matte or fringe; no binary-alpha rule imposed.

requirements.name: ready-meaning
requirements.check: Viewed alone, Ready visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion; it reads as completion rather than activity, failure, pause, or the idle Start control.
requirements.reason: Viewed native and 3x: a short descending left arm joins a distinctly longer ascending right arm into a clear check mark. It reads as successful completion rather than triangle, pause bars, loop or failure.

requirements.name: readability-1x-3x
requirements.check: Composited on #172336, the silhouette is readable at 1x and at 3x nearest-neighbor scale, with no essential detail lost into the panel colour.
requirements.reason: Native 16x16 panel composite shows a recognizable light-blue check; 48x48 nearest composite preserves clear steps and essential asymmetrical arms against #172336.

requirements.name: cool-blue-accent
requirements.check: The dominant colour treatment visibly relates to the existing UI's cool blue accent as seen in assets/start.svg (#70b9ed). This is a visual relationship judgement, not an exact-hex or palette-count rule.
requirements.reason: Visible sky-blue treatment relates directly to the preserved Start SVG's cool-blue cue; measured color happens to equal #70b9ed, but exact equality was not a rejection rule.

requirements.name: sample-pixel-craft
requirements.check: As a representative family sample, the image shows deliberate pixel-art construction: clean pixel clusters and edges, no noisy stray pixels, blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts, and a treatment that could plausibly be extended to Working, Retry and Paused.
requirements.reason: Viewed all native and enlarged views: compact connected stepped clusters form a crisp check without blur, isolated noise or downscaled illustration artifacts. A plausible sample for future family extension; family adoption and comparisons remain separate.

1	# Candidate inspection and retained review
2	
3	Use this operation to review an existing saved raster candidate. The project owns
4	the requirements; PIXL supplies the observation and judgment. The runtime prepares
5	exact inputs, reports measurements, and retains the review. Read the implemented
6	[inspection contract](../../../resources/spec/candidate-inspection.md) for closed
7	request schemas and result fields.

9	## Prepare from saved requirements
10	
11	Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT` and `inspection STATE --root ROOT` before repeating
12	work. Resolve the candidate X, its output F, contract C and required Q. Save applicable
13	criteria before preparing views. If requirements or source bytes have changed, retain
14	the earlier result and prepare a fresh packet against the amended saved plan.
15	
16	When forming or amending criteria, apply the [authority check](intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules).
17	Retain the supporting project requirement or proposal through the verdict; an observed
18	reference property or diagnostic threshold does not become an adopted rejection rule.
19	
20	Choose actual reference S/X IDs, an integer enlargement and useful backgrounds.
21	An empty reference list is explicit. For animation or tiles, supply the known decoded
22	frame and actual rectangles/timing/pivots or tile neighborhood. Unknown timing and
23	pivots stay null. These options describe how to inspect this project, not a new style
24	contract. Example options for an existing reference ID:
25	
26	```json
27	{"references":["reference"],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff","#202838"],"max_side":1024,"contexts":[]}
28	```

30	Run `inspection-prepare STORE CANDIDATE PACKET OPTIONS_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`
31	or `pixl_inspection_prepare`. Use a fresh packet ID and the actual current state hash.
32	The packet retains original bytes, exact decoded frames, native views, nearest-neighbor
33	enlargements, explicit contexts, measurements and the original acceptance conditions.
34	Read its result to locate the prepared files and view IDs.

36	## View, then judge
37	
38	When the host file viewer omits delivery metadata, use `pixl_inspection` with
39	`path`, `packet_id` and `view_ids` (1–8 prepared IDs per call). It returns the
40	actual selected PNG image blocks plus matching hashes and `payload_size` dimensions,
41	without resizing. View/forward the image blocks, not only their text metadata.
42	Those dimensions describe this transmitted image payload; record any later host
43	resizing separately, and keep delivery unknown if the host transforms it without
44	reporting the result. A tool result alone does not establish that anyone viewed it.
45	
46	Open the retained candidate and reference views with the host's image viewer. Inspect
47	native readability and enlarged structure on the selected backgrounds. Use individual
48	views or complete crops for large inputs; a nominal 1x cell in a resized sheet is not
49	native-scale viewing. Read animation or tile contexts where the saved criteria require
50	them. A frame strip retains poses and declared timing; it does not establish playback
51	or target-engine behavior.
52	
53	For a repository consumer, start with its existing isolated renderer or integration
54	runner. Retain actual rendered frames, timing and state transitions, then inspect
55	the saved native/enlarged pixels. A headless run can supply actual execution and
56	playback observations without taking control of the user's desktop. Use interactive
57	computer control only when it adds an observation the project runner cannot provide.
58	
59	If one viewer or browser fails, use another suitable observation route before
60	declaring the check unavailable. Review recorded playback as a sequence, including
61	every required phase and the wrap; distinguish it from a synthetic frame strip.
62	Check for throttling or skipped phases in the recording. Judge the specific motion
63	condition from adequate visual and temporal evidence; do not invent a human-only
64	real-time viewing requirement. Measurements support the specialist's visual
65	judgment and do not create it automatically.
66	
67	Record the view IDs actually seen, what each showed and the dimensions delivered by
68	the host when known. Use `delivered_size: null` when delivery dimensions are unknown;
69	file dimensions alone do not establish the viewer's delivered dimensions. Report any
70	resizing. Complete native and enlarged coverage at prepared dimensions is required
71	for a visual/continuity pass. An observed candidate defect can justify failure before
72	all views have been inspected; retain at least the actual candidate view and report
73	the partial coverage honestly. A reference-only observation does not inspect the candidate.
74	
75	Interpret measurements against the saved criteria. A dimension/palette/alpha result
76	is mechanical evidence. Component counts, edge differences and reference colors are
77	observations whose artistic meaning depends on the project. Compare the actual
78	required features before a visual verdict. Omit unperformed criteria or explicitly
79	record an unavailable check with its concrete reason. This local operation can record
80	engine/live criteria only as unavailable; actual external acceptance uses its own
81	execution evidence.
82	
83	## Retain and continue
84	
85	For actual external observations (recorded motion, collective family views or
86	destination execution), use the [candidate/family review operation](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md).
87	Read `review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` first.
88	It supplies exact literal criteria, current verdict IDs, semantic `binding_hash`
89	and canonical `state_hash`. Save explicit observation JSON, then call
90	`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
91	or `pixl_candidate_review`. It handles a raster or family manifest and derives
92	evidence records while retaining exact observation files. Use an existing reviewer
93	actor, actual observation time, explicit reasons and observations of the required
94	mode. Do not reuse prior review prose as a claim of new viewing.
95	
96	Choose `action: "record"`, `"nominate"` or `"complete"` deliberately. Partial,
97	failed and unavailable checks remain useful records. Completion preserves all
98	prerequisite, selection, pending-job and acceptance checks. After interruption,
99	reload state and repeat the identical review ID/JSON; the retained review is reused
100	and outstanding publication finishes without duplicate verdicts. Do not construct
101	E/V records by hand for this ordinary operation. Prepared inspection-packet review
102	below retains its existing coverage rules; this external-observation route does
103	not certify that a packet was viewed completely.
104	
105	Write the closed review object described in the contract: saved reviewer A,
106	timezone-aware `observed_at`, actual view observations, explicit per-criterion
107	verdicts/reasons, next action and limitations. Record the observation time after
108	viewing. Use `supersedes: null` for a first verdict; replacing a current verdict must
109	name that exact V. Use a fresh review ID and the latest state hash with
110	`inspection-review STORE PACKET REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`
111	or `pixl_inspection_review`.
112	
113	The operation retains its report and creates bound E/V for supplied performed checks.
114	It preserves failures and unavailable checks without nominating a candidate or marking
115	the task done. Read `inspection` and `workflow` again. Once all required checks and assigned integration are complete, use `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` with the accepted candidate IDs; then confirm the saved task is done. A revision is a new candidate;
116	it begins with unperformed criteria and cannot inherit the rejected candidate's pass.
117	If scope drift blocks review, amend the plan through the existing lifecycle rules and
118	prepare fresh views. Do not relabel the old observation as current evidence.
119	
120	Finish with the actual result, the next useful action and any unresolved requirement.
121	Cold resumption uses the retained inspection report to recover the exact old inputs,
122	criterion text, declared viewing limits and next action. Continue through
123	[sample acceptance](intake-sample.md) or [family production](family-delivery.md) as
124	appropriate. Successful publication verifies retention, not whether a host truly
125	looked or an engine accepted the asset.
